text:
Bitcoin remained pinned near the $62,000 threshold the evening of June 23, finalizing a bruising session dominated by a synchronized global tech liquidation. Capital violently rotated out of AI-linked equities, dragging the Nasdaq down 2% and cratering South Korea's KOSPI by nearly 10%. Institutional crypto allocators aggressively compounded this downside, pushing 30-day net outflows across spot ETFs, corporate treasuries, and stablecoins to a staggering $8 billion.

Amidst this broader risk-off environment, BlackRock counter-maneuvered by launching the iShares Bitcoin Premium Income ETF (BITA), targeting a 15–25% annual yield through active covered calls.

This acute digital asset weakness is tethered to surging macroeconomic headwinds. With the May Producer Price Index spiking 6.5% year-over-year and the 10-year Treasury yield stubbornly anchored at 4.49%, an increasingly hawkish Federal Reserve outlook is systemically draining liquidity from risk assets.
